item.title: What to Expect in Your First Online Tutoring Session
item.description: A first session can feel uncertain. Here is what usually happens, what to bring, and how to make the most of your time.

item.title: How to Study for a Test in One Week
item.description: Limited time doesn't have to mean panic. A focused seven-day plan puts your effort where it will help most.

item.title: Active Recall: Why Testing Yourself Beats Rereading
item.description: Rereading feels productive, yet testing yourself is one of the most reliable ways to learn. Here is why, and how to start.

item.title: How to Read a Syllabus and Plan Your Semester
item.description: Your syllabus holds the dates, grading rules, and expectations for the whole term. Here is how to turn it into a plan.

item.title: How to Write a Strong Thesis Statement
item.description: A strong thesis gives your essay a clear direction. Here is how to write one that your body paragraphs can support.

item.title: APA In-Text Citations: A Practical Guide
item.description: In-text citations connect your claims to your sources. Here is how to format them in APA style, with examples you can adapt.

item.title: Algebra Homework Help That Builds Real Skills
item.description: Homework help should make you better at algebra, not just finish the set. Here is how to get that benefit without copying answers.

item.title: A Four-Week Study Plan for Standardized Tests
item.description: Four weeks is enough time for steady, measurable progress. This plan moves from diagnosis to full practice in a clear sequence.
